summary: The smallest development block, a Residential Mixed Use site on Exposition Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard next to China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry, capped at 120 ft. It was in the original Phase 1 but was swapped out for Parcel F in 2019 to bring about 100 more units into the first phase; it remains unbuilt.

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA and Design Controls that set this block's use and envelope (Resolutions 18-03, 18-04)
Board of Supervisors affirms the EIR certification and approvals (Resolution 33-18); Notice of Determination filed March 9, 2018
Development Agreement and DDA take effect; DA term 30 years, project planned in up to four phases
Draft EIR's illustrative phasing placed Block K in Area 1 with Blocks A and G, China Basin Park and Pier 48, 2017-2020
Developer proposes moving Parcel K to a later phase and bringing Parcel F into Phase 1 instead, for about 100 more units, about 40 more affordable, and a four-corner intersection
Port Commission approves the Phase 1 budget with the K-for-F swap, finding it meets the DDA's criteria for a phase boundary change (Resolution 19-39)
Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal (with a Garage Report submitted October 14, 2022 and a Basis of Design November 18, 2022); the budget and appraisal elements are deferred
Port Commission finds Phase 2 'not currently financially feasible'; Port and developer agree to decelerate Phase 2 work while monitoring the market (Resolution 23-46)

Port staff say later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to reach the project's 40% target after Phase 1 was cut to 132 BMR units; the Port, developer and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'to improve the feasibility of future Phases' (Resolution 25-17)

open_questions: The geometry file quotes the Design Controls as saying 'the shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park'; that sentence was not found in the April 2018 Design Controls text or the D4D, though the 120-ft cap is confirmed by the Block K standards page.
The swap's stated reasons (units, affordable units, intersection form) are documented; no source mentions interim-parking preservation as a reason.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block K. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) placed Parcel K in Phase 1 in its original Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5), before the 2019 swap moved it out; the September 2019 Phase 1 budget staff report says only that the swap 'moves parcel K to a later phase' without naming which one, and no document read states K's post-swap phase number or gives it a target date. Even the pre-swap Phase 1 slot is moot now that K itself was removed from Phase 1, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a date for this block.
